tasks.objective: Establish the true onset and blast radius of the incident from telemetry, independent of the 40-minute report. For settlement-service and its consumer group, report: exact timestamp when settlement consumer lag first began rising and when processed-message throughput dropped to zero (from metrics/logs), plus any errors/signatures in settlement-service logs at onset. Then check whether other services consuming from or producing to the same topic/queue show anomalies in the same window, and whether broker/queue-level metrics (produce rate, partition health) changed at onset. Answer: is this settlement-service-local or is it a shared/upstream signal?
tasks.answer: The incident is NOT what the 08:22 report implies (no settlements for ~40 min). True onset is ~07:40Z: settlement-service consumer_lag was flat ~40-55 until the 07:35 bucket, then jumped to avg 515 at 07:40 and rose monotonically to ~60k by 09:55; processed throughput (request_rate) collapsed from ~62 req/s to ~0.4 req/s between 07:40 and 07:54. The trigger signature is local-partition deserialization failure: from 07:42:14Z settlement-service repeatedly fails on ONE partition/offset (orders-3@8841207): 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)', followed by 'poison message ... partition blocked' — so the consumer is stuck on a single bad/schema-mismatched message. Blast radius: the consumer-side damage is confined to settlement-service's partition orders-3 (all 213 errors + 196 poison logs reference that one key), while upstream order-service stayed healthy on INFO in the same window but had a deployment to v2.16.0 complete at 07:40:01Z, ~2 min before the first consumer error. On the evidence available, the malformed v2-schema message entering the orders topic is a shared/upstream signal (producer side), but the stall itself is local to settlement-service's consumer group; I could not directly read broker-level metrics to confirm whether other consumer groups saw the same bad message.

Historical precedents (HIST-112, HIST-104) both point to broker/partition-assignment causes, so the poll-settings change is not the only plausible explanation. Downstream logs/metrics and the kafka broker view are needed to discriminate.
